text: My goldfish just got its learner's permit and needs me in the passenger seat.
My fridge and washing machine have declared independence. I have to attend their first cabinet meeting.
My pillow has issued a final warning: report to bed immediately or lose all blanket privileges.
The Wi-Fi is celebrating its birthday and has requested an hour of silence from all connected devices.
My shadow clocked out early. I need to catch it before it takes the last bus home.
I spilled coffee on my keyboard. Now it will only type 'one more espresso'.
The moon is short-staffed tonight. I've been called in to hold the flashlight.
My cat called an emergency board meeting. The motion to log me off passed unanimously.
My noodles have scheduled a mandatory meeting, and the agenda is getting soggy.
My social battery has reached 1%. Emergency blanket mode is now activating.
My alarm clocks have formed a union. I need to negotiate a later starting time.
A cloud outside claims it knows my primary school teacher. I need to investigate.
My brain's cache is full. Scheduled maintenance will take approximately one entire night.
The bathroom ducks are hosting a secret disco, and apparently I'm the designated DJ.
My houseplant has learned to walk and is making a break for the front door.
Reality is dropping frames. I need to step outside and install a patch.
A pigeon tapped on my window. The translation app says my dinner is getting cold.
My chair has ended its shift and refuses to provide any more competitive seating.
My headset just forecast a severe pillow storm. I'm heading to bed for shelter.
Tomorrow-me sent an email asking today-me to log off before we both regret it.
The lift in my building has started telling dad jokes. I need to talk it down.
My mouse pad has relocated to the edge of the desk and needs help with its visa paperwork.
Galactic customer service says I've exceeded my daily fun allowance and must log off for an audit.
My duvet has challenged me to a boss fight. The only available move is sleep.
Sleep has chosen me for tonight's main quest: close both eyes and remain offline.
NASA just promoted my duvet to mission commander. It has ordered an immediate return to bed.
My imaginary dragon swallowed the house keys. I need to negotiate a very warm refund.
The council of kitchen spoons has summoned me. Apparently I stirred up a constitutional crisis.
My future self arrived in a tiny spaceship and confiscated my remaining screen time.
I'd join, but my last brain cell has booked a silent retreat and taken the password with it.
Not this round. My gaming licence has been temporarily revoked by a committee of sleepy penguins.
I promised a nervous asteroid I'd watch its first orbit tonight. It has terrible separation anxiety.
My social battery is running on one emergency potato. I can't risk another match.
I'd love to, but my calendar has been eaten by a time-travelling goat. Every appointment is now yesterday.
I'm sitting this one out. My thumbs have formed a union and rejected the overtime proposal.
A wizard has put me on airplane mode. The only available spell is 'do not disturb'.
Not tonight. My imaginary yacht is sinking and all the imaginary lifeboats require a captain.
I have to cancel our plan. My goldfish accidentally became mayor and needs a campaign manager.
Small change of plans: my sofa has opened a portal, and customer support says I must stay for the technician.
I can't make it after all. A time traveller borrowed this evening and returned a Tuesday from 1847.
The plan is cancelled on my end. My laundry has reached sentience and is demanding diplomatic recognition.
I need to cancel. My fridge has begun its opera debut, and I'm the entire audience.
I can't make our session. My houseplant is getting married and insists I walk it down the windowsill.
My plans have been abducted by aliens. They promised to return them after a short survey.
I have to cancel. My calendar challenged a black hole to arm wrestling and lost the whole evening.
It's not my fault. My mouse has clearly chosen violence today.
You need to blame the Wi-Fi. The packets stopped halfway to admire a butterfly.
My keyboard translated 'retreat' into 'perform a dramatic solo entrance'. I'm filing a complaint.
That wasn't a missed shot. Gravity changed its terms and conditions without notifying me.
My monitor is showing the director's cut. Everyone else apparently got the useful version.
The lag is powered by a hamster who just discovered paid leave.
My controller outsourced that move to a confused toaster. We are reviewing the contract.
The hitbox briefly moved to another postcode. I respect its privacy, but I object to the timing.
Give me a minute. My coffee is still installing its courage update.
I'll be a little late. My shoes have entered a staring contest and neither side will blink.
Hold on. My last brain cell is circling the car park looking for the entrance.
A tiny dragon is warming up my keyboard. It refuses to skip the safety briefing.
I need a few minutes. My internet packets are waiting for a very small ferry.
Be right there. My chair is completing its pre-flight checklist.
Give me a moment. The microwave has started a countdown and refuses to explain the mission.
I'm almost ready. My loading screen hired another loading screen to cover its lunch break.
